external_data.name: EUROCONTROL Performance Review Unit, All-causes pre-departure delay (airport, day)
external_data.terms_and_nature: as recorded in configs/daily_totals_v1.json: not an open licence; per airport and off-block day the sum of max(off-block - schedule, 0), an aggregate of the hidden clock of the ranking rows. No official score and no leaderboard information is used.

procedure.summary: the procedure of configs/daily_totals_v1.json, and in addition the heavy rows (sd of their positive-delay error above 900 s: fill candidates and similar), which v1 leaves at their prediction, move by a tempered posterior: the likelihood of the day's published total without the row, at each of the row's outcomes, enters to the power heavy_temper. A heavy row never receives the day shift. Amendment: a heavy row that holds an NM off-block clock keeps its prediction.
procedure.heavy_prior: bounded: the row's outcomes without a visible delay (label at least the schedule interval minus 120 s: fills, off-block before schedule, one-day labels) count as the schedule interval, because the total tells a delay from none and cannot tell those outcomes apart; the outcomes with and without delay keep their cell's proportions inside their group and the two groups' weights make the mean the row's prediction (reconcile.group_weights). A row predicted above its schedule interval, or below the mean of its delay outcomes, holds one hypothesis and is not moved between the two. The heavy rows are the rows that are heavy under v1's weights.
procedure.pins: a heavy row predicted within 120 s of its schedule interval (a declared fill) keeps its prediction
procedure.bound: by construction a heavy row moves between the mean of its delay outcomes and its schedule interval, never beyond
procedure.fitting_side: as v1: cells, the published figure's accuracy and the day-shift scale per airport from the months other than the one read
procedure.free_parameters: heavy_temper, declared per candidate; nothing fitted on scores or on the scored months

temper_10.note: the strength the user's word covers; v2's governing run read -0.160 / -0.129 / -0.194 / -0.215% without the amendment

development_read.control: the declared procedure of configs/daily_totals_v1.json on the v46 development stack (its governing run, docs/daily_totals/results_v1.json)
development_read.construction: for each month, the fitting side from the other three months
development_read.rule: the candidate passes when no equal-footing month is worse than the control on all rows, the mean change over them is at least 0.02% below zero and every equal-footing month's paired-day 95% interval (by off-block day, seed 20260929) lies below zero. November is reported. The expectation is the v2 result within a few thousandths of a percent, that is: every month better and the rule not passed.
development_read.expectation_disclosed: as v2: the intervals of July and December are expected to include zero

prior_exploration_disclosed.learned_model: a LightGBM residual model with the published features, read as f(x, delta) - f(x, 0) and applied to the LIRF population rows on top of v1: -0.354 / -0.315 / -0.349 / -0.280% against v1 on the four months; with the days' discrepancies permuted within airport-month no gain. It showed that a moderate response to the day's discrepancy works where the exact posterior does not.
prior_exploration_disclosed.development_stack_earlier_prior: tempered posterior with the exponential-tilt prior, all airports, against v1: power 0.10: -0.207 / -0.052 / -0.565 / -0.043% (intervals below zero in January and November); power 0.25: -0.314 / +0.041 / -0.825 / +0.147%; first-order tilt for heavy rows: +2.9 / +9.1 / -0.2% (three months run). All of the change is on the LIRF fill population; heavy rows at other airports move by seconds.
prior_exploration_disclosed.twelve_month_table: runs/daily_totals/rows12p.parquet: the twelve-month table of the v1 check with the LIRF fill population in every month (1,487 rows; the 950 population rows that the cross-fit tables lack enter with a leave-one-month-out v9 mixture). LIRF's airport-days only, against v1's procedure on the same table. Exponential-tilt prior: power 0.05 -0.207%, 0.10 -0.339%, 0.25 -0.536% (mean over twelve months, each 12 of 12 better). Two-group prior with pins: 0.10 -0.363%, 0.25 -0.587% (12 of 12). Bounded prior with pins (the declared form): 0.10 -0.310% (12 of 12, ten intervals below zero), 0.25 -0.519% (12 of 12, nine intervals below zero), 1.00 -0.810% (11 of 12; July +0.50%).
prior_exploration_disclosed.placebo: each day reads another day's discrepancy of the same airport-month: bounded prior, power 0.25: mean -0.137%, 7 of 12 months better. About half of the population's gain survives the placebo: a day's ordinary discrepancy, whichever day, excludes a delay of many hours. The true totals are better than the placebo on the population rows in 12 of 12 months.
prior_exploration_disclosed.why_the_prior_changed: a label-free look at the ranking rows: with the exponential-tilt prior the largest moves (+1,500 to +2,500 s) fell on rows predicted at or above their schedule interval, among them v40's fill pins, because that prior gives such rows about a fifth of one-day weight. The two-group prior, the pins and the bound remove this. The look used no label and no score.

amendment.change: heavy_keep_clock: a heavy row that holds an NM off-block clock keeps its prediction; it still enters the day's arithmetic
amendment.reason: the procedure's evidence is on the LIRF fill population, which by definition holds no NM record. The class that carries the population's cells also holds rows with an NM record (17 of 400 on the ranking rows, 25 of 562 in the development months). In development their moves are worth 0.7e6 of squared error against 124e6 on the population. On the ranking rows one of them, a departure whose NM clocks lie one day before its takeoff and whose prediction follows that clock (85,975 s; schedule interval 94,560 s), moved by +2,617 s and carried 6.9e6 of v49's 17.1e6 squared change against v48. No development row of that kind exists. A row with an NM clock is not a fill candidate hedged between a delay and none, and the population's cells do not describe it.
amendment.found_by: an independent label-free check of the built v49 against the supplied ranking columns (clocks, aircraft type) and the earlier files
